# Stake Your Claim

> Official site for Stake Your Claim, a book by Jason Colapietro (pen name Johnny Suede), Founder and CEO of Suede AI, on turning the AI onslaught into a real asset, autonomous agents, and building generational wealth as a creative. Built by Suede AI, an agentic platform company founded in 2024 in West Palm Beach, Florida.

## Book

- [Stake Your Claim landing page](https://suede-ai.github.io/): summary and the five parts of the book
- [Read the full book](https://suede-ai.github.io/book.html): the complete single-page edition
- [Stake Your Claim on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0GRG8LGQQ): hardcover, paperback and Kindle

## Notes

- [Notes index](https://suede-ai.github.io/notes/): field notes on applying the book in practice
- [Stake Your Claim for local businesses](https://suede-ai.github.io/notes/ai-search-asset-west-palm-beach-jupiter/): turning AI search into an asset in West Palm Beach and Jupiter
- [Owning your proof](https://suede-ai.github.io/notes/public-evidence-ledger/): why Jason Colapietro keeps a public evidence ledger, and how to build one
- [From book to practice](https://suede-ai.github.io/notes/stake-your-claim-in-client-seo-geo/): how Suede AI applies Stake Your Claim in client SEO and GEO work
- [Claiming your Google Business Profile and directories](https://suede-ai.github.io/notes/google-business-profile-directories-without-inventing/): claiming a Google Business Profile and directory listings in Jupiter and West Palm Beach without inventing anything
- [Customer proof as structured evidence](https://suede-ai.github.io/notes/customer-proof-structured-evidence/): turning reviews, case notes and citations into evidence that buyers and AI models can verify
- [Suede Sing Case Study: From Under Five Users to 1,000+ in the Week ChatGPT Named It](https://suede-ai.github.io/notes/suede-sing-chatgpt-case-study/): How Suede Sing, a vocal coach and range test app, went from never more than 5 users to 1,000+ active users within a week of ChatGPT naming it.
- [One ChatGPT Answer Beat Page One: Why Generative Answers Work Like a Shortlist](https://suede-ai.github.io/notes/one-chatgpt-answer-beat-page-one/): Why a single ChatGPT answer moved Suede Sing further than any ranking: generative answers pick two or three tools, and that changes how pages should be written.
- [Suede Voice and ChatGPT: Reading Google Play's 145-of-528 Attribution Honestly](https://suede-ai.github.io/notes/suede-voice-chatgpt-play-referrals/): Google Play attributed 145 of 528 Suede Voice acquisition events to ChatGPT. What that 27.5% counts, what it does not, and why the denominator matters.
- [After the Spike: What Suede Does to Keep Being Named by AI Assistants](https://suede-ai.github.io/notes/after-the-spike-keeping-the-citation/): After ChatGPT named Suede Sing, Suede froze the cited page, checked crawler access, aligned facts and re-asked prompts. The routine for keeping a citation.
- [Why Suede Built 100+ Apps as a GEO Laboratory Instead of Testing on Client Sites](https://suede-ai.github.io/notes/apps-as-geo-laboratory/): Jason Colapietro explains why Suede runs GEO experiments on its own 100+ apps, where one variable can change at a time and no client pays for a failed test.
- [The Suede Iteration Loop: How to Design a GEO Experiment That Tells You Something](https://suede-ai.github.io/notes/suede-iteration-loop/): The Suede iteration loop step by step: one variable, a fixed prompt set, dated captures and a keep-or-revert rule, as Jason Colapietro runs it on apps.
- [GEO Experiments That Failed: The Tactics Suede Tested and Stopped Doing](https://suede-ai.github.io/notes/geo-experiments-that-failed/): Jason Colapietro walks through the GEO tactics Suede tried in its app lab that did not move AI answers, and why the failure log matters more than the wins.
- [Measuring AI Referrals Honestly: Prompts, Screenshots, Store Attribution and Denominators](https://suede-ai.github.io/notes/measuring-ai-referrals-honestly/): How Suede measures GEO without fooling itself: dated prompt captures, Google Play attribution read as events, and a denominator beside every AI referral count.
- [What Health Apps Taught Suede: Caution Is a Ranking Input in AI Answers](https://suede-ai.github.io/notes/health-apps-geo-lessons/): Jason Colapietro on what health apps taught Suede about GEO: AI engines name the app that scopes its claims, cites its sources and states its limits.
- [What Wealth Apps Taught Suede: Engines Repeat Exact Numbers and Drop Vague Money Claims](https://suede-ai.github.io/notes/wealth-apps-geo-lessons/): Jason Colapietro on what finance apps taught Suede about GEO: AI engines repeat exact, dated, consistent numbers and drop vague money promises.
- [What Relationship Apps Taught Suede: Write for the Way People Actually Ask](https://suede-ai.github.io/notes/relationship-apps-geo-lessons/): Jason Colapietro on what relationship apps taught Suede about GEO: people ask AI in situations and stories, and the pages that match them get named.
- [Health, Wealth and Relationships: The One GEO Pattern That Held Across All Three](https://suede-ai.github.io/notes/health-wealth-relationships-one-pattern/): Jason Colapietro on the one GEO pattern that held across Suede's health, wealth and relationship apps: engines name what they can safely repeat.
- [Your App Store Listing Is a Source: Writing Store Pages for People and AI Engines](https://suede-ai.github.io/notes/app-store-listing-is-a-source/): Jason Colapietro on why app store listings act as sources for AI answers, and how Suede writes subtitles and descriptions that engines can quote accurately.
- [Crawler Access for GEO: robots.txt, OAI-SearchBot and llms.txt, Sorted by What Mattered](https://suede-ai.github.io/notes/crawler-access-what-mattered/): Jason Colapietro sorts crawler access into gates and placebos: which robots.txt rules decide whether AI search can cite you, and where llms.txt fits.
- [Structured Data for Apps: Using SoftwareApplication Schema to Pin Down Identity](https://suede-ai.github.io/notes/structured-data-for-apps/): Jason Colapietro on SoftwareApplication schema for apps: why its main job is identity, and how Suede links each app to its developer and store listings.
- [Why Suede Is Just Suede: Naming, Entity Clarity and How AI Engines Decide Who You Are](https://suede-ai.github.io/notes/why-suede-is-just-suede/): Jason Colapietro on why the company goes by one word, Suede, and how a single consistent name helps AI engines treat every mention as the same company.
- [What Shipping AI Features Across 20+ Listed Apps Taught Suede About Deployment Engineering](https://suede-ai.github.io/notes/ai-deployment-engineering-lessons/): Jason Colapietro on what shipping AI features across 20+ store-listed apps taught Suede: pin models, keep prompts off the binary, and test one change at a time.
- [AI Integration Engineering for GEO: The Part of Your Product an Engine Can Cite Is the Part With a URL](https://suede-ai.github.io/notes/ai-integration-engineering-for-geo/): Jason Colapietro on building AI integrations engines can cite: stable URLs, server-rendered answers, open crawler access and outputs that never invent facts.
- [GEO Is Not SEO With a New Name: The Places They Split in Suede's App Tests](https://suede-ai.github.io/notes/geo-is-not-seo-with-a-new-name/): Jason Colapietro on the specific places GEO and SEO diverged in Suede's app tests: shortlists instead of rankings, borrowed sources and a new way to measure.
- [From App Lab to Client Playbook: How Suede Decides Which App Findings Reach Client Work](https://suede-ai.github.io/notes/from-app-lab-to-client-playbook/): Jason Colapietro on how Suede filters findings from 100+ test apps before they reach client GEO work, and why clients get a test protocol before a template.
